The drumheads are natural animal skin, mostly cowhide or goatskin, treated specially to improve the tone. The beater is made of bamboo or light wood, with small balls at the ends, commonly of clay, wooden beads or ivory. The cord joining the beaters to the body is hemp or silk, which keeps it flexible and durable. Some higher-grade instruments have fine decoration on the wooden parts.

The rattle drum is a membranophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 212. It usually has two drumheads with two beaters attached by cord; in China, Korea and Japan it is mostly mounted on a straight handle, and turning the handle makes the beaters strike the heads. There are also hourglass and barrel shapes, and several drums can share one handle. Its uses include religious ritual and secular settings: in Tibet, Mongolia, India and Taiwan it is used in ritual, and small versions serve as children's toys or the rattles of street vendors; China's tao and bolanggu appear in ritual music and among pedlars, Korea has single- to four-drum versions, Japan uses it as a toy drum, and Thailand uses it in royal ritual. The South Asian hand drum is made of two skullcaps glued together and serves as a ritual instrument in Hinduism, Bon and Tibetan Buddhism.
搖鼓的基本操作是先握住鼓下木柄或鼓腰，使鼓面朝外；再以手腕左右搖擺，或依器形大小: The basic method is to grip the wooden handle below the drum, or the waist of the drum, with the head facing out, then swing the wrist from side to side, or, depending on the size, turn the handle along its axis so that the beaters on their cords strike the head in rhythm. Beginners can start with the single-drum type, holding the handle in one hand and swinging it left and right; in the double-drum type the smaller drum sits above and the larger below, and shaking it sounds the drums and the yunluo (cloud gongs) in the iron ring at the same time.
搖鼓的實際使用場合主要見於宗教儀式與世俗響器。來源指出，此類鼓常見於西藏、蒙古、: In practice the rattle drum is used mainly in religious ritual and as a secular rattle. The source notes that this kind of drum is common in the religious rituals of Tibet, Mongolia, India and Taiwan; the South Asian hand drum also serves as a ritual instrument in Hinduism, Bon and Tibetan Buddhism. Thailand uses this kind of drum in royal ritual. Small versions in China and East Asia are mostly children's toys or the rattles of street vendors, for example the cloth sellers and the needle-and-thread pedlars of recent Chinese history. For Korea's single-, double-, triple- and four-drum rattle drums the source marks only that they are used in Korea and does not describe the occasions.
搖鼓的歷史可追溯至戰國時期，作為打擊樂器，見於東亞、南亞部分地區與南美洲，發展出: The history of the rattle drum can be traced back to the Warring States period; as a percussion instrument it is found in East Asia, parts of South Asia and South America, and has developed into various types and sizes. In China, Korea and Japan the drum is mostly fixed to or threaded on a vertical handle, and turning it makes the pellets strike the head; Tibet, Mongolia and India use the damaru, and Thailand has the Glong banthoh for court ritual. It is also used in religious ritual, especially in Tibet, Mongolia, India and Taiwan; small versions became children's toys or vendors' rattles in East Asia. In recent Chinese history the single-drum bolanggu was the sign of the cloth seller, and the double-drum huolanggu was used by pedlars carrying needle and thread. The South Asian hand drum is made of two human skullcaps glued together and serves as a ritual instrument in Hinduism, Bon and Tibetan Buddhism.
搖鼓音色清脆明亮，具有輕快靈動的質感。當演奏者搖晃樂器時，連接的槌子撞擊鼓面，產: The rattle drum's timbre is clear and bright, with a light, nimble quality. When the player shakes the instrument, the attached beaters strike the head and produce a penetrating stroke; the range lies mainly in the middle and upper register, with a strong sense of direction and focus. Its resonance is distinctive: the two opposing heads form a resonating chamber that gives the sound a bright ring. Beside the deep dullness of a bass drum the rattle drum is lighter and more springing; beside the sharp edge of a triangle it has more of a warm membrane quality. Its ability to strike rapidly and repeatedly gives the sound rhythm and swing, and it is often used to create a relaxed, cheerful or festive atmosphere.
